title: CRED Founder Kunal Shah Named to Lead WhatsApp in Meta's Biggest India Bet Yet
excerpt: Meta taps one of India's most prominent entrepreneurs to run its 3.3-billion-user messaging platform, pairing the appointment with a $900 million investment in Shah's fintech startup.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Kunal Shah replaces Will Cathcart as WhatsApp's global head, marking a significant leadership change.
  • Meta invests $900 million in CRED, valuing it at $4.5 billion and acquiring 20% ownership.
  • WhatsApp has over 500 million users in India, its largest market, highlighting its growth potential.
  • Shah's leadership aims to enhance WhatsApp's business messaging and digital payments capabilities.

Meta's investment details
  • Kunal Shah, founder of Indian fintech giant CRED, replaces Will Cathcart as the global head of WhatsApp
  • Meta is simultaneously investing $900 million in CRED at a $4.5 billion valuation, acquiring roughly 20% of the company
  • Shah's appointment puts an Indian entrepreneur at the helm of the world's largest messaging platform, which counts India as its biggest market with 500+ million users
  • The move signals Meta's intent to unlock WhatsApp's unrealized potential in business messaging and digital payments

Meta Platforms has named Kunal Shah, the founder of Indian fintech company CRED, as the new global head of WhatsApp, placing one of India's most recognized entrepreneurs in charge of the world's largest messaging service with 3.3 billion monthly active users.

Shah replaces Will Cathcart, who led WhatsApp for nearly seven years and oversaw its expansion beyond private messaging into Communities, Channels, and AI integrations. Cathcart will move to a new role at Meta focused on building consumer products from scratch.

A Cold Email That Changed Everything

The appointment traces back to a cold outreach from Meta Chief Product Officer Chris Cox, who had been canvassing entrepreneurs and investors across India, Brazil, and Mexico — countries where WhatsApp is a dominant force in commerce and culture.

"The deal values the fintech company at $4.5 billion post-money and gives Meta roughly 20% ownership.</p> <p>Shah will step down as CRED's CEO while retaining his personal shareholding."

"He had an incredible set of answers. At the end of the call, I asked him if maybe he and I should talk about him doing it."

— Chris Cox, Meta Chief Product Officer

Cox's search for a leader who understood WhatsApp's global product opportunity led to dinner with Mark Zuckerberg. "Kunal built Cred into one of India's most important technology companies, and he brings the kind of builder mentality and global perspective that will serve him well in running the world's biggest messaging app," Zuckerberg said.

The $900 Million CRED Deal

The leadership change comes alongside a Meta-led $900 million financing round for CRED, structured through a combination of primary and secondary share purchases. The deal values the fintech company at $4.5 billion post-money and gives Meta roughly 20% ownership.

WhatsApp's User Landscape in India
›WhatsApp's largest market is India with over 500 million users.
›WhatsApp Pay faces competition from PhonePe and Google Pay.
›Despite 3 billion global users, WhatsApp's business model is underdeveloped.

Shah will step down as CRED's CEO while retaining his personal shareholding. Miten Sampat, who leads strategy and finance at CRED, will serve as interim CEO while the board works on longer-term leadership ahead of an eventual IPO.

India Is the Prize

India is WhatsApp's largest market, with more than 500 million users. The country has emerged as a key battleground for Meta's ambitions in business messaging and digital payments — areas seen as critical to WhatsApp's next phase of growth.

While WhatsApp Pay gained traction in India, the service has struggled to replicate the scale of local rivals like PhonePe and Google Pay. Despite an audience of over three billion monthly users globally, WhatsApp's business model remains relatively underdeveloped for its size.

Diaspora Angle

Shah's unconventional path — he studied philosophy at Mumbai's Wilson College and dropped out of an MBA program — has sparked widespread discussion about meritocracy in tech. He previously built and sold FreeCharge for approximately $450 million before founding CRED, which grew to 17 million members.

"While it's come very far, the delta between WhatsApp today and its full potential is massive."

— Kunal Shah, incoming WhatsApp head

What's Next

Shah joins Meta's global leadership team at a time when the company is aggressively investing in AI agents and business tools. WhatsApp currently generates billions from paid messaging and ads that push users into business chats, but is still rolling out subscriptions and AI agent features. For the Indian diaspora, having an Indian founder at the helm of one of the most widely used communication tools worldwide represents a landmark moment in tech leadership.
